row.evidence: Databricks' SCIM docs say "Your Databricks account must have the Premium plan or above", and its pricing page says the Standard tier is discontinued for new customers on AWS and Google Cloud, making Premium the entry tier.
row.notes: Status changed gated -> free: Standard is discontinued for new customers on AWS/GCP (existing Standard accounts were moved to Premium on Oct 1, 2025), so SCIM sits on the entry (Premium) tier with no upcharge; June's own row already had multiplier 1.0. Usage-based DBU pricing, so per-user fields are null; June's '~$0.55/DBU' could not be found on the current page and was replaced with the listed 'starting at $0.15/DBU' (Data Engineering). Azure Databricks pricing is set by Microsoft and was not re-checked. Account SCIM for Okta, Entra, OneLogin, JumpCloud; deprovisioning deactivates (tokens blocked, objects kept). Entra automatic identity management is an alternative sync. Enterprise adds compliance features; ESC add-on is 15% of spend.

plans.name: Premium
plans.price_text: Usage-based, pay-as-you-go per DBU; e.g. Data Engineering starting at $0.15/DBU
plans.notes: Lowest tier for new customers on AWS and GCP (Standard discontinued). Audit logs listed on Premium; queried via system tables, not a REST endpoint.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.price_text: Usage-based per DBU (higher DBU rates; contact sales for commits)
plans.notes: Adds advanced compliance and security; Enhanced Security and Compliance add-on is 15% of product spend.

auth.token_source: Account console > Security > Identity provider setup > Enable user provisioning (SCIM token + Account SCIM URL)
auth.notes: Token can be regenerated; old token keeps working for 24 hours. API calls also accept OAuth with the 'scim' scope.

endpoints.notes: Service principals also have SCIM endpoints.

deprovision.data_retained: Deactivation keeps permissions and objects; user tokens remain but cannot authenticate; compute keeps running; scheduled jobs fail unless reassigned. Deleting via Okta deletes the user; OneLogin 'Delete' archives resources irreversibly.

filtering.notes: Operators eq, co, sw, ne with and/or; max 200 nodes in a filter expression.

pagination.notes: count is documented as '<= 100' while the description says the default is 10000.

custom.how: Only a fixed set of nine identity attributes (Beta) can be provisioned on account SCIM 2.1.

roles.how: SCIM 'roles' attribute on users and groups (admin role); entitlements can be provisioned from the IdP; workspace assignment managed in Databricks.

rate_limits.text: Account SCIM API: 20 GET/s, 240 LIST/min, 2 PATCH/s, 5 POST/PUT/DELETE/s; max 10,000 users+service principals and 5,000 groups per account.

limitations.text: Usernames and email addresses cannot be updated; userName and emails.value must match.
Groups cannot be renamed; Entra group name changes do not sync.
Entra SCIM connector cannot sync nested groups or service principals (automatic identity management can).
OneLogin cannot create groups in Databricks.

scim.notes: Account-level SCIM is recommended; workspace-level SCIM (/api/2.0/preview/scim/v2) is legacy Public Preview. API reference documents /api/2.0/accounts/{account_id}/scim/v2; docs call the newer surface 'account SCIM 2.1' at /api/2.1/. SSO is recommended, not required.

auth.notes: Method list beyond the 'scim' API scope not separately cited.

audit_log_api.notes: Audit logs are queried through the audit log system table (Public Preview) or log delivery, not a dedicated REST endpoint.

rate_limits.text: Account SCIM API: 20 GET/s, 240 LIST/min, 2 PATCH/s, 5 POST/PUT/DELETE/s.

user_api.notes: Databricks' user-management API is its SCIM API (Account Users/Groups/Service Principals, plus legacy workspace SCIM); there is no separate non-SCIM user API.

okta.notes: OIN page marks SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push and Group Linking as checked (read from page markup).

entra.notes: Gallery app 'Azure Databricks SCIM Provisioning Connector' per Databricks docs; Microsoft Learn tutorial not checked. Entra automatic identity management is a separate vendor-run sync.

onelogin.notes: From Databricks' OneLogin guide; OneLogin catalogue not loaded (bot challenge).

fallbacks.other_sync: Automatic identity management (Microsoft Entra ID sync, including nested groups and service principals)

open_questions: Docs do not say whether deactivated users stop counting toward any seat or user limit (pricing is usage-based, not per seat).
API reference shows /api/2.0/accounts/.../scim/v2 while the identity-attributes page and Users page use /api/2.1/; whether 2.0 is deprecated is not stated.
Google Workspace provisioning to Databricks is not documented on AWS docs.
Azure Databricks still lists tiers via Microsoft; whether Azure Standard has been retired was not verified.
Whether ServiceProviderConfig/Schemas endpoints exist is not documented in the API reference.
